## Design

### 2026-10-06: Date:  October 5, 2026

**2h**

Date:  October 5, 2026

I started by going through the Starbie guide to get everything set up. I was able to download some files, but others took patience and required tutorial videos to resolve the issue. The most difficult files to download were the .sym and .pretty files, since they required other platforms like KiCad to run first. It was a tough process trying to familiarize myself with all the software, but it was manageable and made me feel more confident when starting to design my starbie project.

### 2026-10-07: Date: October 6, 2026

**2h**

Date: October 6, 2026

In this session, I continued working on the Starbie PCB guide by starting the schematic design. I had to lay out all the parts, including the buttons, sensors, mainboard, resistor, and connection pins. I wired all the parts using the green wire function and used labels to create the SCL and SDA connections virtually. In the beginning, I spent some time getting more familiar with the features and ran into some problems where parts would duplicate, which sometimes caused me to delete them and restart. After making sure all the parts were connected properly, I moved on to assigning the footprints. At first, I had to do some research about the parts being used and looked at the sample bill of materials to help assign the correct footprint to each part. Once I looked at the image in the guide, I was able to confirm that I had assigned the correct footprints.

![part layout](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/B5xWFG6gm7WgdrhdULmY6PTXmJFExRos/1669507ef34824501a9f55422a25657a9d36c26015a402b92b73a7be2395afc8.png)

### 2026-10-10: Date: October 9, 2026

**2h**

Date: October 9, 2026

In this session, I worked on routing the PCB and designing the boundary in a shape of a star. At the beginning, it was hard for me to rearrange the PCB layout, but I used the guided image to roughly place the parts in the right place. When routing the PCB, I used two colors, red and blue. The red were the main lines that the guide image showed how to route and the blue were the additional connections to complete the wiring outline. The blue was mainly used for the GND or ground connections. I also had to look up videos that showed how to make the boundary in the shape of a star and I used the line function to make the stair shaped outline. Sometimes when I was outlining, the line function would stop and I would just continue making lines that didn't connect. So I looked for the pattern of how it worked and I was able to complete the shape without any disconnections.

![PCB routing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/B5xWFG6gm7WgdrhdULmY6PTXmJFExRos/124b8c648557b5df79ca251211b19b8f2d100dece9a96f59c0004e65c4662a3b.png)

![shape design](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/B5xWFG6gm7WgdrhdULmY6PTXmJFExRos/2f147b2ce7eabf9589c0caacc777aa4a5aa8a85a0c46d6e71ef3b588053bc582.png)

### 2026-10-11: Date: October 10, 2026

**3h**

Date: October 10, 2026

In this session, I worked on downloading and setting up the Arduino IDE so I could begin programming Starbie. While installing the ESP32 board, I ran into an issue where the installer kept repeating that the component was already installed and then tried to install it again. I decided to uninstall and reinstall the software, which fixed the loop and allowed me to finish downloading the remaining files. After everything was installed, I opened Starbie.ino and started customizing Starbie's functions, including changing its actions to Dance and Love. I also added the code for the Starbie special effect.

![special effect code add-on](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/B5xWFG6gm7WgdrhdULmY6PTXmJFExRos/bbf5ad3228604c964abb6fb186547ff7db02f4e3c4d8c1c51d14c084b344cd90.png)

![esp32 board installation](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/B5xWFG6gm7WgdrhdULmY6PTXmJFExRos/08a9b00ed62586fc9d32a285c619d2b73f1015517cd02408cf4af22aa9ac6490.png)

### 2026-10-11: Date: October 11, 2026

**4h**

Date: October 11, 2026

In this session, I worked on adding a bitmap pet image to my code. I started by looking for an animal image and decided to use a panda. I used the provided website to edit the image and generate code that would work with Arduino IDE. I also exported the Gerber and drill files for my custom PCB and worked on estimating the project costs. While working on the bill of materials, I was confused about how the prices were listed, but I figured out that I needed to list the price for each part I needed. Estimating the tax was also difficult because I did not know the final shipping cost, so I looked up an estimated tax amount to calculate an approximate value. Finally, I organized all the information needed for my project submission.
